metadata.name: Ear wax (cerumen) impaction
metadata.severity: Mild; causes hearing loss/discomfort but not dangerous

overview.short_description: Accumulation of cerumen obstructing the ear canal, causing hearing loss, blockage, discomfort or tinnitus, easily managed with softening drops and irrigation/microsuction.
overview.detailed_description: A very common, benign reason for reduced hearing in primary care. It is often precipitated by cotton-bud use, hearing aids or narrow canals. Management is softening (cerumenolytic) drops followed by irrigation or microsuction. The main task is to confirm wax is the cause of symptoms and exclude other causes of hearing loss or ear pathology.
overview.pathophysiology: Normal self-clearing of cerumen fails (excess production, narrow/tortuous canal, pushed-in wax, foreign devices), so wax accumulates and occludes the canal, attenuating sound transmission.
overview.etiology: Impaired cerumen clearance; cotton buds, hearing aids/ear plugs, hairy or narrow canals, older age.
overview.natural_history: Gradual build-up; resolves promptly with removal.
overview.prognosis: Excellent; may recur, especially in hearing-aid users.

prevalence.value: Very common; a frequent cause of reversible hearing loss in older adults and hearing-aid users.

epidemiology.age_groups: All ages; more troublesome in the elderly.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Cotton-bud use, in-ear devices (earphones), water exposure.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Canal anatomy; dry vs wet cerumen types.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Recurrent impaction; hearing aids; prior ear surgery/perforation (affects removal method).

symptoms.symptom: Hearing loss (conductive) in the affected ear

symptoms.importance: May accompany; consider other causes if persists after removal

symptoms.symptom: Wax visibly occluding the canal on otoscopy

negative_findings.finding: Hearing loss persists after wax removal
negative_findings.why_important: Indicates another cause of hearing loss needing assessment
Absence argues against infection/other ear pathology

history_questions.why_ask: Wax often unilateral/gradual; sudden loss needs urgent assessment

history_questions.question: Any pain, discharge, vertigo, or a known perforation/ear surgery?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Wax occluding the canal; drum not visible

physical_examination.examination: Recheck otoscopy and hearing after removal
physical_examination.expected_finding: Clear canal, visible drum, improved hearing

physical_examination.examination: Basic hearing assessment (whisper/tuning fork if needed)
physical_examination.expected_finding: Conductive pattern that resolves with removal

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Microsuction (by trained clinician) for removal, especially if perforation/mastoid cavity
other_diagnostic_tests.audiometry: If hearing loss persists after wax removal

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Clinical: symptoms (hearing loss/blockage) with otoscopic confirmation of wax occluding the canal, and improvement after removal.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Pain on ear manipulation, inflamed canal, discharge
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the ear painful or discharging?

differential_diagnosis.red_flags: Unilateral effusion in adult (exclude nasopharyngeal tumour)
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: After removing wax, is hearing normal?
Was anything put in the ear?

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the hearing loss come on suddenly, and is there vertigo?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Do not miss a time-critical sensorineural loss
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Sudden loss -> urgent ENT referral, not simply wax removal

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there a known eardrum perforation or previous ear surgery?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: If perforation/surgery -> avoid irrigation, use microsuction

next_best_question.current_situation: Reduced hearing with wax on otoscopy
next_best_question.question: Was the loss gradual, and do you have a perforation, pain, discharge, or sudden onset?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Simple gradual wax vs red-flag features
next_best_question.branching_logic: Gradual, no red flags -> softening drops then irrigation/microsuction; sudden loss -> urgent ENT; perforation -> microsuction not irrigation

next_best_test.why: Confirms wax as the cause and success of removal
If hearing loss persists after wax removal

red_flags.finding: Sudden hearing loss (especially unilateral) with a clear canal
red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent ENT - suspected sudden sensorineural hearing loss (time-critical)
Reassess for infection before/instead of routine wax removal

red_flags.finding: Vertigo, facial weakness, or neurological symptoms
Persistent unilateral hearing loss/effusion in an adult

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss; suspected serious ear pathology.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Wax not removable in primary care (needs microsuction), or persistent hearing loss after removal for audiology.

early: Minor canal trauma or otitis externa from removal attempts

initial_management.supportive_care: Reassurance; confirm wax is the cause.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Cerumenolytic; Irrigation; Manual removal/microsuction. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: AAOHNS_CERUMEN_2017.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Do not use cotton buds; use softening drops periodically if prone to build-up (especially hearing-aid users).
initial_management.follow_up: Re-check hearing after removal; audiology if hearing loss persists.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Cerumenolytic drops (e.g., olive oil, sodium bicarbonate, or proprietary drops) for several days to soften wax; then ear irrigation or microsuction if needed. Avoid irrigation if perforation, previous ear surgery, or active infection - use microsuction instead.

patient_education.home_advice: Ear wax build-up is harmless and a common cause of a blocked, muffled ear. Softening drops (like olive oil) for a few days often help it clear; sometimes the nurse needs to flush or suction it out. Never poke cotton buds into your ear, as this pushes wax deeper. See a doctor promptly if your hearing drops suddenly, or you have pain, discharge, or dizziness.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: تراكم صملاخ الأذن غير خطير وسبب شائع لانسداد الأذن وضعف السمع. تُفيد قطرات التليين (كزيت الزيتون) لبضعة أيام، وقد يحتاج الأمر أحياناً إلى غسل أو شفط في العيادة. لا تُدخل أعواد القطن في الأذن فهي تدفع الشمع أعمق. راجع الطبيب سريعاً إذا هبط سمعك فجأةً، أو ظهر ألم أو إفراز أو دوخة.
patient_education.prevention: Avoid cotton buds; regular softening drops for those prone to build-up.
patient_education.warning_signs: Sudden hearing loss, ear pain, discharge, dizziness, or hearing that stays reduced after wax removal.

prevention.lifestyle: Avoid cotton buds; periodic softening drops if prone.
